events.title: Investigation assessment
events.detail: The current incident involves HTTP 503 errors in the checkout service, with no origin diagnostics available. Policy enforcement blocks all recovery actions—rollback, feature flag disable, and service restart—due to the absence of origin logs and request traces. The dependency topology shows checkout depends on payments and inventory, which in turn depend on ledger and notifications. Historical incident memory (INC-2041) indicates that a payments feature flag (strict_currency_validation) was the root cause, but this outcome is not currently applicable due to missing diagnostic evidence. Without origin-level telemetry, no action is justified by current evidence. A full diagnosis requires origin logs and request traces to validate the failure origin and rule out service-level or configuration issues.

INC-2043
data.summary: Checkout requests return HTTP 503. Origin telemetry is unavailable.

Checkout 503 errors are caused by payments v2.4's strict_currency_validation rejecting legacy currency strings. The dependency graph shows payments failure impacts checkout and storefront. Ledger schema 1 advisory permits rollback to payments v2.3. No flag-only mitigation is allowed per current policy. Probe confirms payments is unhealthy with same validation error. All required evidence is present and consistent.

Payments v2.4's strict_currency_validation is rejecting legacy currency strings, causing checkout and storefront failures. Ledger schema 2 is active and blocks rollback to v2.3. The runtime flag can be disabled to restore compatibility without deployment rollback. All impacted services (checkout, storefront, inventory, notifications) are affected via dependency chains. Probing confirms inventory and ledger are healthy, and the root cause is in payments' validation logic. Disabling the flag is permitted by current policy and will restore legacy currency acceptance.
